name: emma-read
comment: The emma guest (app/src/PrismEmma.lex.tex) answers three requests, each a verb, a line end and a body. 'check' and a document answers 'malformed', or 'conforms' or 'violates' with assertion ids. 'read' and a document answers 'malformed', 'other' when the document is not one the writer writes, else its lines. 'input' and lines answers the document those lines describe, 'invalid' when the lines are not in the grammar, or 'refused' and the checker's report when the document they describe would break an assertion: the writer never answers a document its own checker faults. The lines: 'ns <uri>' first, when the payload has a namespace; 'stage <id>' opens an interpretation inside emma:derivation, 'best <id>' the interpretation (or emma:one-of member) that is a child of emma:emma, 'choice <id>' an emma:one-of; 'set <annotation> <value>' gives the open element an emma: annotation; 'from <id>' or 'from <id> composite' an emma:derived-from; 'field <name> <text>' a payload element, which 'set' lines then annotate and 'attr <name> <value>' lines give attributes ('attr xmlns <uri>' its own namespace, 'attr xml:<name> <value>' an attribute of XML's own); 'literal <text>' an emma:literal. No document of the Recommendation that has the writer's shape carries an 'attr' line, so no vector here holds that line. Values write a backslash, line feed, carriage return and tab as two characters. This set: 'read' of each of the 28 documents of the Recommendation (pinned in app/specs/emma/spec.json, same ordinals) that already have the writer's shape: interpretations with flat payload fields (annotated or not) or a literal, alone, in one emma:one-of, or staged through emma:derivation. The lines were also reached by a conforming XML parser reading the same bytes, outside the guest.

  <emma:one-of id="r1" emma:start="1087995961542" emma:end="1087995963542"
     emma:medium="acoustic" emma:mode="voice">
    <emma:interpretation id="int1" emma:confidence="0.75"
    emma:tokens="flights from boston to denver">

      <destination>Denver</destination>
